Mobile by the numbers

What kind of city is Mobile, Alabama?

Mobile is a Gulf Coast port city at the head of Mobile Bay, founded in 1702 by Pierre Le Moyne and Jean-Baptiste Le Moyne as part of French Louisiana. It had 187,041 residents at the 2020 census and an estimate of 204,689 after an annexation in 2023, which makes it the second most populous city in Alabama.

The city covers 180.07 square miles, of which 40.59 square miles is water, and its elevation runs from 10 feet on Water Street downtown to 211 feet at Mobile Regional Airport. That spread is the whole story for property owners: a few blocks can separate a house that floods from one that stays dry.

Mobile city factFigure
Founded1702
Incorporated as a cityDecember 17, 1819
Total area180.07 square miles
Elevation range10 feet to 211 feet
Population, 2020 census187,041
Form of governmentMayor-Council

Mobile is also known for Mardi Gras, said to be the oldest organized Carnival celebration in the United States, and it is home to several art museums, a symphony orchestra and a large concentration of historic architecture.

Which Mobile neighborhoods are historic districts?

Mobile has a long list of historic neighborhoods: Ashland Place, Campground, Church Street East, De Tonti Square, Leinkauf, Lower Dauphin Street, Midtown, Oakleigh Garden, Old Dauphin Way, Spring Hill and Toulminville.

Many of those areas contain houses a century old or more. If you own one, a buyer or lender may ask about the roof, wiring, plumbing and foundation, and the repair bill can eat into what a retail sale would net. Selling as-is to a cash buyer skips that negotiation.

  • Midtown took the worst of the December 25, 2012 tornado, with damage to at least 100 structures.
  • Streets named in that damage report included Carlen Street, Rickarby Place, Dauphin Street, Old Shell Road, Margaret Street, Silverwood Street and Springhill Avenue.

Who bills property tax on a house in the city of Mobile?

The Mobile County Revenue Commission bills and collects property tax on houses inside the city. The commission's offices are closed on Wednesdays.

Property tax in Alabama is due October 1 and turns delinquent after December 31. If it goes unpaid, the state timetable has the delinquent list reach probate court in February, the property advertised for sale in April, and a tax sale in May.

Because school systems differ, two houses in the same county can have different totals. Mobile County Public School System covers most of the county, but Chickasaw, Saraland and Satsuma run their own systems, which matters if your address is near those lines.

The commission publishes its details at mobilecopropertytax.com.

What does the Mobile climate do to a house?

Mobile is the wettest city in the lower 48 states by one 2007 study, at 66.3 inches of average annual rainfall, so roofs, gutters and crawl spaces take constant punishment. July and August are the wettest months, and snow is rare, although January 21, 2025 brought up to 8.5 inches.

Storm history is long. Hurricane Frederic crossed the city in 1979 as a Category 3 storm. Opal in 1995 and Ivan in 2004 caused moderate damage, and Katrina's storm surge of 11.45 feet flooded downtown and the elevated Jubilee Parkway in 2005. Hurricane Sally in 2020 was a Category 2 that moved slowly through Alabama, and Zeta hit a month later.

The record high temperature is 106 degrees Fahrenheit, set on August 26, 2023, and the record low is negative 1 degree, set in 1899. In a house, the heat and humidity matter more than the cold: air conditioning, moisture and mold are the things inspectors check.

How do the port and local employers affect Mobile house sales?

Mobile's economy rests on the Port of Mobile, aerospace, shipbuilding, steel, medicine and retail. The port is the 12th largest in the nation, Austal USA began aluminum shipbuilding in 1999, BAE Systems Southeast Shipyards employs about 600 people on Pinto Island, and the Brookley Aeroplex hosts more than 70 companies.

Airbus opened its first U.S. A320 family assembly plant in Mobile in 2015, and it began A220 production in 2019. The University of South Alabama, a research university with more than 16,000 students, is based in the county.

Industry shifts can change where people want to live and how fast houses sell.

How do roads and the wider region connect Mobile?

Interstate 10 enters the Wallace Tunnel in Mobile, and Interstates 65 and 165 also serve the county. U.S. Highway 90 crosses the Mobile River on the Cochrane-Africatown USA Bridge, and The Wave Transit System runs local buses.

The city is the center of a metro area of about 412,000 people. Together with the Daphne-Fairhope-Foley area, it forms a combined area of 665,147 people, according to the city's Wikipedia entry. Mobile surrendered to Union forces in April 1865 after losses at two forts that protected the city,.

For a seller, the region matters because port, shipyard and aerospace employers draw workers who may look at houses in the city.

What is the transfer and recording process for a Mobile house?

A Mobile deed is recorded with the county probate office, and Alabama Code 40-22-1 charges a recording privilege tax of $0.50 for every $500 of value. The instrument must come with a form stating the real sale price, and a false or missing value can bring a penalty of $100 or 25% of the tax, whichever is greater.

Two thirds of the deed tax goes to the state and one third to the county. On a $150,000 Mobile sale, the tax is $150.

  • Pay or clear the current tax balance, which is normally done at closing.
  • Sign a deed that matches the legal description in the county records.
  • Submit the sale price form with the deed.
  • The buyer then assesses the house in their own name with the Revenue Commission.

How do you challenge a Mobile assessment?

You can challenge an assessed value through the county Board of Equalization, and anyone who disagrees with the board's final decision has 30 days to appeal to circuit court under Alabama Code 40-3-25. The taxpayer must give notice to the board secretary and the circuit clerk and file a bond.

The same statute requires the taxpayer to pay prior-year taxes before they go delinquent, or the court can dismiss the appeal. A seller who files an appeal and stops paying risks losing it.

The statute is posted on Justia.

What do Mobile sellers usually face?

Typical Mobile sellers have an older house, storm wear and a tax or probate question. Inheritance is common in historic neighborhoods where families have held a house for decades, and a house can sit while an estate gets opened. Mobile County counted 184,441 housing units in 2020, and 11.2% of them were vacant, so empty houses are a visible part of the market.

Cash Home Buyers purchases Mobile houses as-is, including houses with tax due, deferred repairs or storm damage. The title company pays any balance owed from the proceeds.

More questions about Mobile, AL Property Tax Guide

Who sends the property tax bill for a house in Mobile, Alabama?

The Mobile County Revenue Commission bills and collects the tax. Its offices are closed on Wednesdays.

When is property tax due in Mobile?

October 1 each year, with delinquency after December 31. A tax sale can follow in May if the bill remains unpaid.

How wet is Mobile, Alabama?

A 2007 study found Mobile averaged 66.3 inches of rain a year, which made it the wettest city in the contiguous 48 states.

What is the deed tax on a Mobile house sale?

Alabama Code 40-22-1 sets it at $0.50 per $500 of value, so a $200,000 sale would carry $200 of deed tax.

Can I sell my Mobile house if it has hurricane damage?

Yes. A cash buyer can purchase the house in its current condition, and any unpaid tax comes out of the closing proceeds.

Montgomery by the numbers

What should you know about Montgomery, Alabama, before selling a house there?

Montgomery is Alabama's capital, a river city on the Alabama River with 200,603 residents at the 2020 census. It was incorporated on December 3, 1819, replaced Tuscaloosa as state capital in 1846, and sits at about 220 feet above sea level on rolling terrain.

The city covers 162.27 square miles, almost all of it land, and Montgomery is the county seat of Montgomery County. The metro area counted 385,460 people in 2022, and the city's own estimate for 2023 was 195,287.

Montgomery city factFigure
IncorporatedDecember 3, 1819
State capital since1846
Total area162.27 square miles (2.41 water)
Population, 2020 census200,603
Metro population, 2022385,460
GovernmentMayor-Council

Who are the largest employers in Montgomery?

Maxwell-Gunter Air Force Base and the State of Alabama are the two biggest employers in Montgomery. According to the city's 2022 annual financial report, as quoted in Wikipedia, Maxwell-Gunter employs 12,280 people and the state government 10,315.

EmployerEmployees
Maxwell-Gunter Air Force Base12,280
State of Alabama10,315
Montgomery Public Schools4,524
Baptist Health4,300
Hyundai Motor Manufacturing Alabama3,530
ALFA Companies2,568

Government work, healthcare and manufacturing give Montgomery a steadier base than a single-industry town. The city has also long been a distribution hub because of its river, interstates and rail lines, and it draws workers from outside, with daytime population rising 17.4% to 239,101.

Who bills property tax on a Montgomery house?

The Montgomery County Revenue Commissioner assesses and bills property tax for houses in the city. Property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, and from there the state's timetable runs to the probate court in February, a newspaper advertisement in April, and a tax sale in May.

Notices of value come from the county Board of Equalization. For the 2024 tax year, the county said it expected to mail notices by the fourth week of May 2024, and the lien date was October 1, 2023. Those are 2024 figures taken from the county's appeals FAQ, so check the office for the year you are in.

  • Due: October 1.
  • Delinquent: after December 31.
  • Appeal window: 30 days from the date printed on the notice.
  • Filing fee: none, according to the county.

Details are on the county's appeals page.

How do you appeal a Montgomery property value?

You appeal by sending a request to the county, with supporting documents, within 30 days of the date printed on your notice. The county says there is no fee, no required form, and that an informal review before the Board of Equalization is available and recommended.

Requests go to propertytaxappeals@mc-ala.org, and the real property appeals line is (334) 832-1327. The Board of Equalization wants all supporting documents filed with the appeal, and it asks for original signatures. It may ask for closing statements, appraisals, comparable sales and insurance values.

For the 2024 tax year, the board looked at sales from October 1, 2022 through September 30, 2023. An out-of-state representative can file for an owner, an attorney is not required, and the representative must supply a signed authorization form.

After a board ruling, state law gives 30 days to appeal to circuit court under Alabama Code 40-3-25, and the taxpayer must keep paying prior-year taxes on time while the case continues.

What does the Montgomery climate mean for a house?

Montgomery has a humid subtropical climate with long, hot summers and short, mild winters. Highs exceed 90 degrees on about 86 days a year, and summer heat indexes are often at or above 100.

Spring thunderstorms can bring large hail, damaging wind and tornado risk, and tropical systems that weaken inland can bring very heavy rain. For a house, that makes the roof the first thing an inspector will look at, followed by drainage and the air conditioning unit.

  • Average July temperature: 81.8 degrees Fahrenheit.
  • Average January temperature: 46.6 degrees Fahrenheit.
  • Wettest months: February, March and July.
  • Driest month: October.

Substantial snowstorms happen roughly once every ten years, so freeze damage is a lesser concern than heat and storms.

How do roads and universities affect where buyers want to live?

Montgomery is on two interstates, I-65 and I-85, and I-85 ends in the city. Montgomery Regional Airport has flights to hubs including Atlanta, Houston-Intercontinental and Charlotte, and the Montgomery Area Transit System runs local buses.

Alabama State University, Auburn University at Montgomery, Troy University's Montgomery campus, Faulkner University and Huntingdon College are all here. Montgomery Public Schools serves most of the county, while Pike Road City School District runs the schools in Pike Road, and Maxwell Air Force Base is zoned to Defense Department schools for elementary and middle grades.

The city has been recognized for downtown revitalization and was one of the first in the nation to adopt SmartCode zoning.

How does Montgomery County surround the city?

Montgomery County was created on December 6, 1816, covers 800 square miles, and had 228,954 residents in 2020, making it the seventh most populous county in Alabama. Montgomery is its seat and largest municipality, and Hope Hull and Pike Road are the only towns besides it.

The county borders Elmore, Macon, Bullock, Pike, Crenshaw, Lowndes and Autauga counties. U.S. Highways 31, 80, 82, 231 and 331 cross it along with the two interstates.

The county's own housing count in 2020 was 105,293 units and 56.3% of occupied homes were owner-occupied. A seller in an unincorporated community such as Pintlala, Snowdoun or Mount Meigs still deals with the same county Revenue Commissioner as a seller downtown.

Downtown Montgomery lies on the south bank of the Alabama River about 6 miles below where the Coosa and Tallapoosa rivers meet. The Alabama State Capitol stands on a hill at the end of Dexter Avenue, and the 375 foot RSA Tower is the tallest feature of the skyline. Montgomery was also the first capital of the Confederacy in February 1861 and a major site in the civil rights movement, including the bus boycott and the Selma to Montgomery marches.

What does the sale and recording process look like in Montgomery?

A Montgomery deed is recorded with the probate judge, and Alabama Code 40-22-1 requires the recording privilege tax of $0.50 per $500 of value before the deed is accepted. The deed has to come with a form stating the real purchase price.

The unpaid property tax, if any, comes out of the seller's proceeds, handled by the title company. Montgomery County's own numbers show why this matters: 43.7% of occupied housing units in the county were renter-occupied in 2020, so many sellers are landlords with rentals that may carry arrears.

  • Request a payoff figure from the Revenue Commissioner.
  • Collect the deed, the closing statement and any survey.
  • File the deed with the probate judge after closing.
  • New owners should assess the house in their own name.

What do Montgomery sellers usually face?

Montgomery sellers often hold inherited houses, rentals or older homes that need work. The county had 105,293 housing units in 2020, and 11.5% were vacant, which means empty houses are a normal part of the landscape.

Cash Home Buyers buys Montgomery houses as-is, including those with back taxes, and the title company pays any unpaid property tax from the proceeds.

More questions about Montgomery, AL Property Tax Guide

Who sends Montgomery, Alabama property tax bills?

The Montgomery County Revenue Commissioner assesses and bills property tax for houses inside the city of Montgomery.

When is Montgomery property tax due?

Property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, under the Alabama Department of Revenue calendar.

How long do I have to appeal my Montgomery property value?

You have 30 days from the date printed on your notice, and the county says there is no filing fee.

What documents help a Montgomery appeal?

The county names closing statements, appraisals, comparable sales and insurance values as examples, and the board wants them filed with the appeal.

Can I sell a Montgomery house that has unpaid property tax?

Yes. The balance is paid from the proceeds at closing, so get a payoff figure from the Revenue Commissioner first.

Tuscaloosa by the numbers

Where is Tuscaloosa, Alabama?

Tuscaloosa is the county seat of Tuscaloosa County, in west-central Alabama on the Black Warrior River, about 60 miles southwest of Birmingham. It sits on the fall line, where the Gulf Coastal and Piedmont plains meet, so the ground runs from forested hills in the northeast to low, marshy plain in the southwest.

The city covers 72.22 square miles, of which 62.15 are land and 10.07 are water. Most of that water is Lake Tuscaloosa, which lies entirely inside the city limits, plus the river. The elevation is 190 feet.

ZIP codes in the city include 35401 through 35407, plus 35486 and 35487, and the area codes are 205 and 659. Those details help when you check which parcel, school zone or tax area a house falls in.

Why is Tuscaloosa called the Druid City?

The nickname Druid City comes from the many water oaks planted along downtown streets starting in the 1840s. Other nicknames are T-Town and, after the Alabama football titles in 2009, 2011, 2012, 2015, 2017 and 2020, the City of Champions.

The town was incorporated on December 13, 1819, and was spelled Tuskaloosa until the early twentieth century. It served as Alabama's capital from 1826 to 1846, and the old State House stood at the corner of 6th Street and 28th Avenue, now Capitol Park.

How many people live in Tuscaloosa?

Tuscaloosa had 99,600 residents in the 2020 census and was estimated at 114,288 in 2025, which makes it Alabama's fifth most populous city. The 2020 count was a 10.1 percent rise from 2010.

Census yearPopulation
199077,759
200077,906
201090,468
202099,600
2025 (estimate)114,288

The city had almost no growth in the 1990s and then added about 12,500 people in the 2000s and about 9,100 in the 2010s, by simple subtraction of the census counts.

Which neighborhoods make up the city?

Wikipedia lists these major areas of Tuscaloosa proper:

  • Alberta
  • Central and Midtown Tuscaloosa
  • Downtown Tuscaloosa
  • East Tuscaloosa
  • Hillcrest
  • North River
  • The University of Alabama main campus
  • West Tuscaloosa

The retail center sits around 15th Street and McFarland Boulevard, home to The Shoppes at Legacy Park, University Mall and Midtown Village. Houses near campus, near the retail corridor and along the river can each sell to a different kind of buyer.

What is the climate in Tuscaloosa, and what does it mean for a house?

Tuscaloosa has a humid subtropical climate, with summers that last from mid-May to mid-September and winters that run from mid-December to late February. Rain is abundant, which is worth remembering when you look at roofs and gutters.

MeasureFigure
January average daily temperature44.7 °F
July average daily temperature81.7 °F
Days with highs of 90 °F or more per year71 to 72
Days at 100 °F or more per year3.5
Days at or below freezing per year46
Average seasonal snowfall0.7 inches
Record high at Tuscaloosa Regional Airport107 °F
Record low at Tuscaloosa Regional Airport-1 °F

January and February are the wettest months on average. Severe thunderstorms can bring damaging winds, large hail and occasional tornadoes, and the severe weather seasons peak in spring and fall.

What did the 2011 tornado change?

On April 27, 2011, a wide EF4 tornado hit Tuscaloosa, with top winds estimated at 190 mph, and 44 of the 64 deaths it caused were in the city. It was part of the 2011 Super Outbreak. An EF3 tornado had struck the city twelve days earlier, on April 15.

Total damage from the April 27 tornado came to $2.45 billion, and Mayor Walt Maddox said whole neighborhoods had been removed from the map. For a seller, the practical point is that parts of the city were rebuilt after 2011, so ask when your house was built or repaired and keep any records from that period.

What drives the Tuscaloosa economy?

The University of Alabama is the city's largest employer and, per Wikipedia, generates over $2.5 billion in economic impact each year. Higher education is the foundation, with retail, automotive, manufacturing, health care and public jobs around it.

Mercedes-Benz U.S. International employs more than 6,100 people and supports over 11,000 more jobs through regional suppliers. Brose Tuscaloosa, ARD Logistics and ZF Chassis Systems supply it. Other employers named include JVC America, Nucor Steel, BFGoodrich, Hunt Refining, GAF Materials, The Westervelt Company and gChem.

The University of Alabama, Shelton State Community College and Stillman College together enrolled 43,681 students in spring 2021. A single home football game was estimated at a $25.8 million impact for the area.

Who bills Tuscaloosa property tax?

The Tuscaloosa County Tax Assessor values the property, and the Tuscaloosa County Tax Collector bills and collects, so a Tuscaloosa house is handled by county offices at 714 Greensboro Ave, with the collector in Room 124 and the assessor in Room 108. The collector's main line is (205) 464-8230, and the assessor's is (205) 464-8240.

  • Taxes are due October 1.
  • December 31 is the last day to pay without penalties or interest, and a postmark of that day is accepted.
  • Taxes are delinquent from January 1, when delinquent notices go out.
  • After March 15, personal checks are no longer accepted.
  • The county advertises its online tax sale in April and holds it in the last week of April.

The Alabama Department of Revenue confirms the October 1 and December 31 dates statewide. We did not read a current Tuscaloosa millage figure on an official page, so ask the assessor's office for the rate on your parcel.

How does Tuscaloosa County value a city house?

The county's appraisal staff reviews values on a four-year cycle and also checks yearly changes triggered by building permits, septic permits, recent sales or a taxpayer request. For 2026, valuation notices carried estimated values as of May 1, 2026, and a protest deadline of May 31, 2026.

A written protest goes to the County Board of Equalization, and Alabama allows 30 days from the written notice of valuation. A recently permitted remodel in Tuscaloosa can prompt a value review, so keep the permit paperwork with your sale file.

Which schools serve Tuscaloosa?

Tuscaloosa City Schools serves students who live inside the city limits, while the Tuscaloosa County School System serves those outside. The city system has about 10,000 students in 24 schools, including three high schools: Paul W. Bryant High School, Central High School and Northridge High School.

The city system also runs the Tuscaloosa Career and Technology Academy. A house just across a city boundary can fall in the other system, so check the boundary before you describe a school zone to a buyer.

What do Tuscaloosa sellers run into?

A college town with a tornado history gives sellers a few common problems.

  • Houses used as student or investor rentals that need turnover repairs.
  • Roof, siding and tree damage from storms, with repair records that buyers may ask to see.
  • Heirs who live out of town and need to settle a family house.
  • Back property tax that went to an old mailing address.

With a cash sale, a title company pays any county tax balance from the proceeds and you avoid waiting on a buyer's lender.

More questions about Tuscaloosa, AL Property Tax Guide

When are Tuscaloosa property taxes due?

Property taxes are due October 1, and December 31 is the last day to pay without penalties or interest. Taxes turn delinquent on January 1.

Does the City of Tuscaloosa bill property tax itself?

The county tax offices bill and collect it. Per the county site, the Tax Assessor handles valuation and the Tax Collector at 714 Greensboro Ave, Room 124, handles payment.

How many people live in Tuscaloosa?

The 2020 census counted 99,600 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 114,288.

When is the Tuscaloosa County tax sale?

The county advertises the sale online in April and holds it in the last week of April, online only.

What is the 2026 protest deadline for Tuscaloosa County values?

The county listed May 31, 2026, with estimated values as of May 1, 2026.

Can I sell my Tuscaloosa house with back taxes?

Yes. A title company can get a payoff figure from the Tax Collector and pay the balance from your sale proceeds at closing.

Huntsville by the numbers

Where is Huntsville and how is the city laid out?

Huntsville sits in the Tennessee River valley in northern Alabama, and it is the county seat of Madison County. The city limits also reach into Limestone, Morgan and Marshall counties, which matters when you work out who bills the tax on a particular house.

The city covers about 225 square miles, according to the Wikipedia summary of Census figures, and it is ringed by plateaus and ridges. Monte Sano Mountain rises east of town, with Round Top, Chapman, Green and Wade mountains and others around the edges. Elevation in the city is about 577 feet. Large annexations pushed the boundary west into Limestone County in the early 2000s and south into Morgan County in 2018, and the city added more than 1,000 acres in Marshall County in 2025.

For a seller this means two houses with a Huntsville mailing address can sit in different tax jurisdictions. Check the parcel record before you assume anything about the bill. The Madison County tax collector only bills what lies in Madison County.

ItemDetail
Established as TwickenhamDecember 23, 1809 (renamed Huntsville in 1812)
Incorporated as a cityFebruary 24, 1860
2020 Census population215,006
2025 population estimate233,627, the largest city in Alabama
Counties the city touchesMadison, Limestone, Morgan, Marshall

What does Huntsville's history mean for old houses here?

Huntsville was platted around the Big Spring, so the oldest streets near downtown predate most of the state. LeRoy Pope bought the site and named it Twickenham, and the town took the name Huntsville in 1812 after John Hunt.

Textile mills added a second wave of housing in the 1890s. The Lowe Mill Village and the Lincoln Mill and Mill Village historic districts date from that boom, and the Old Town Historic District holds homes from the late 1820s into the early 1900s. A house inside a historic district can carry design review rules, so ask the city before you plan any exterior work or demolition.

The next big change came after World War II, when Redstone Arsenal turned into a rocket research center. NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center opened in 1960, and subdivisions spread outward from there. A lot of Huntsville's ranch houses and split levels come from that era, and many now need new roofs, wiring and plumbing.

What drives the Huntsville economy?

Aerospace and defense work drive the economy. Redstone Arsenal, Cummings Research Park, the Jetplex Industrial Park and NASA's Marshall center form the main hubs. Cummings Research Park is described as the second largest research park in the country, and the University of Alabama in Huntsville sits in the same orbit.

Manufacturing adds another layer. Toyota Motor Manufacturing Alabama builds engines at the North Huntsville Industrial Park and had 1,800 employees as of 2022. The Mazda Toyota plant, built in 2021, was planned to hire 4,000 people and makes SUVs and pickups. The United States Space Command was selected for Huntsville in 2020, although the headquarters question moved around afterward.

Why this matters to a seller: a household that relocates for a contract, a defense posting or a plant job often has to sell on a deadline. A flexible closing date can matter as much as the price.

How does Huntsville weather affect a house?

Storms are the main risk. Huntsville has a humid subtropical climate, with average yearly precipitation above 54 inches and the wettest stretch running from November to May.

  • Spring and late fall bring the strongest storms, with large hail, straight-line wind and tornadoes.
  • The city sits in the area called Dixie Alley, where long-track tornadoes are more common than in most of the country.
  • The April 27, 2011 Super Outbreak hit northern Alabama.
  • Summer highs run near 90 degrees and winter highs near 49 degrees.

Hail and wind damage show up as roof and siding problems, and buyers who need financing or insurance will ask about them. A cash buyer who accepts the house as it stands avoids that back and forth.

What is the ground like under Huntsville houses?

The land is karst. The city was founded around the Big Spring, a typical karst spring, and caves run through the limestone bedrock beneath the surface. The National Speleological Society is headquartered in Huntsville.

Karst ground can produce sinkholes and drainage surprises. If a house has settling cracks, sticking doors or a soft spot in the yard, expect a retail buyer's inspector to flag it. This is one of the repair surprises that sends Huntsville sellers toward an as-is sale.

Who collects Huntsville property tax, and when is it due?

The Madison County Tax Collector bills and collects property tax for houses in the Madison County part of Huntsville. The state of Alabama says property taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31.

The county explains that a bill covers the period from the previous October 1 through September 30 of the current year. Alabama law does not require a bill before taxes turn delinquent, but the office mails a courtesy notice by October 1 and a final notice after January 1. If nothing arrives, you are still responsible, so call 256-532-3370 or look the parcel up online.

Offices and payment details from the county FAQ:

  • Main office: Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW, Huntsville, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Satellite office: 100 Plaza Blvd., Madison.
  • Cards and debit carry a 2.75 percent convenience fee plus $0.30, and e-checks cost $1.50.
  • In April and May, only certified funds, cash or cards are taken for real property.

What is the Huntsville tax rate, and what does a bill look like?

The county FAQ lists $5.80 per $100 of assessed value for property inside the Huntsville city limits. Madison is listed at $6.95, Triana at $6.15, and New Hope, Gurley and Owens Cross Roads at $4.05. Unincorporated land is listed at $3.35 and improvements at $3.65.

Assessed value starts with the appraised value times the class percentage. Alabama's classes, as laid out by the Lauderdale County revenue office, are 30 percent for utilities, 20 percent for other property and 10 percent for agricultural, timber and owner-occupied single-family homes.

As an illustration only, take a $300,000 owner-occupied house. Ten percent gives $30,000 of assessed value. At the posted $5.80 per $100, that is $1,740 before exemptions. The county's regular homestead worksheet then deducts $48 when assessed value is $4,000 or more, which would leave about $1,692. Your real bill depends on your own appraisal and exemptions, so use this only to see how the pieces fit.

What happens if Huntsville property tax goes unpaid?

A $5.00 late fee applies after December 31, and interest runs at 1 percent per month on the base amount. Probate and advertising fees get added too.

The state timetable runs from delinquency on January 1 to the probate court in February, a probate court meeting in March, advertising in April and a tax sale in May. Madison County holds its annual lien sale online in May.

Paying before the sale is far cheaper than paying after it. If back taxes are the reason you want out of the house, tell the buyer and the title company early so the payoff figure goes on the settlement statement.

How do I challenge my Huntsville assessment?

File a written protest with the Madison County Board of Equalization on the second floor of the Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW. The county cites Code of Alabama sections 40-3-20, 40-3-24 and 40-3-25.

  • New values usually post in March or April, announced by newspaper ad two weeks in a row.
  • You have 30 days from the second ad to appeal.
  • A county appraiser reviews the case first, then a hearing is set if you still disagree.
  • A circuit court appeal must be filed within 30 days after the board adjourns, and the tax must be paid by December 31 or a bond posted for double the tax.

What happens to the tax bill when a Huntsville house sells?

The bill follows the owner of record on October 1 of the previous year, so a buyer can receive a notice in the seller's name. The county tells new owners to confirm the deed is recorded in the probate office at the Madison County Service Center and to assess the property in the Tax Assessor's Office and claim exemptions.

A title company normally prorates the year's tax between buyer and seller at closing. Ask for the proration worksheet, and keep your copy of the paid receipt.

What do Huntsville sellers usually run into?

  • Inherited houses with several heirs and no clear owner of record.
  • Older mill-village and Old Town houses that need major systems work.
  • Hail-damaged roofs from spring storms.
  • Job moves tied to Redstone Arsenal, Cummings Research Park or the auto plants.
  • Delinquent tax on a rental or vacant house.

Each of these is easier with a buyer who closes on your schedule and takes the house in its current condition. Cash Home Buyers makes written offers on Huntsville houses and works with a local title company to clear unpaid tax from the proceeds.

More questions about Huntsville, AL Property Tax Guide

What is the Huntsville property tax rate?

The Madison County Tax Collector's FAQ lists $5.80 per $100 of assessed value inside the Huntsville city limits. Property in the Limestone, Morgan or Marshall portions of the city is billed by those counties, so check your parcel.

When is Huntsville property tax due?

Taxes are due October 1 and become delinquent after December 31. The county mails a courtesy notice by October 1 but does not have to.

Where do I pay property tax in Huntsville?

Pay the Madison County Tax Collector at the Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW, or at the satellite office at 100 Plaza Blvd. in Madison. You can also pay online or by mail, and the main office number is 256-532-3370.

What is the penalty for late property tax in Huntsville?

A $5.00 late fee applies after December 31, plus 1 percent interest per month on the base amount and added probate and advertising costs. Unpaid parcels can go to the May online lien sale.

Can I sell a Huntsville house that owes back taxes?

Yes. The unpaid tax is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the title company will request the payoff figure from the tax collector.

How do I appeal a Huntsville property assessment?

File a written protest with the Madison County Board of Equalization within 30 days of the second newspaper notice of new values. A county appraiser reviews it first, and a hearing follows if needed.

Birmingham by the numbers

Where is Birmingham, Alabama, and what is the city built on?

Birmingham is in the north central part of Alabama, in Jones Valley between long parallel ridges at the southern end of the Appalachian foothills. The Wikipedia article gives the city a total area of about 149.5 square miles and a 2024 population estimate of 196,357, in a metro area of more than 1.19 million people.

Red Mountain lies just south of downtown. Beyond it is Shades Valley and the Over the Mountain suburbs of Mountain Brook, Vestavia Hills, Homewood and Hoover. Ruffner Mountain, east of the city center, holds one of the larger urban nature reserves in the country, and Sand Mountain flanks the city to the north.

The infobox lists two counties for the city, Jefferson and Shelby. Jefferson County is the main one and Birmingham is its county seat, but if your parcel is in the Shelby part you will deal with a different set of county offices. Look at your tax bill to see which county issued it.

ItemDetail
IncorporatedDecember 19, 1871
CountiesJefferson and Shelby
GovernmentMayor and council
Land areaAbout 147 square miles
Metro population1,192,583

What is Birmingham's history in brief?

The Elyton Land Company founded Birmingham in 1871 near the planned crossing of two railroads, close to deposits of iron ore, coal and limestone, the three raw materials of steelmaking. The article says the district is the only place in the world where significant amounts of all three sit close together.

In 1911 the town of Elyton and several other nearby towns were absorbed into the city. The early skyscraper era around 20th Street and 1st Avenue North earned downtown the nickname The Heaviest Corner on Earth. The 1963 civil rights campaign here, which included Martin Luther King Jr.'s Letter from Birmingham Jail, shaped national law.

Because the city grew by merging and annexing, neighborhoods inside it formed at different times, and a buyer will ask when a particular house was built.

What drives Birmingham's economy?

Steel still matters, but healthcare and banking now lead. UAB, established in 1969, is described as the area's largest employer, with a workforce of about 18,750 as of 2011, and its hospital is a Level I trauma center. Regions Financial and Vulcan Materials are headquartered in the area, and Birmingham was the 10th largest banking center in the United States in 2014 by locally headquartered deposits.

  • Steel products: American Cast Iron Pipe Company and McWane are based in the city.
  • Construction and engineering: BE&K, Brasfield and Gorrie, Robins and Morton and B.L. Harbert International appear in national rankings.
  • Colleges: Samford University, Miles College, Jefferson State Community College and Lawson State Community College.

The headquarters of both the Southeastern Conference and the Southwestern Athletic Conference are also listed as being in Birmingham.

What weather risks should a Birmingham homeowner plan for?

Birmingham has a humid subtropical climate with hot summers, mild winters and plenty of rain. Highs reach 90 degrees or more on about 65 days a year, and there are about 47 days a year with a low at or below freezing.

The city sits in what is called Dixie Alley, a region of frequent tornadoes. The article notes two F5 tornadoes hit the greater Birmingham area, in the northern suburbs in 1977 and the western suburbs in 1998, and an EF4 tornado during the April 2011 outbreak. November and early December are a secondary severe weather season.

Roof condition, storm shelter access and insurance claims are therefore normal talking points in a sale. A house with unrepaired storm damage or an open claim needs a clear statement in the contract about who keeps the claim.

What else shapes housing in Birmingham?

Elevation at the city is 597 feet, and the Cahaba River basin south of Shades Valley is described as one of the most diverse river ecosystems in the country. A 5.1 magnitude earthquake near Irondale in 1916 slightly damaged a few buildings, and the area also sees occasional tropical storms and hurricane remnants in late summer and fall because of its proximity to the central Gulf Coast.

  • If your lot is on a slope, expect a buyer's inspector to look at drainage and retaining walls.
  • Keep permits and repair receipts for roof or storm work, because a buyer will ask for them.

When are Birmingham property taxes due and what happens if they are late?

The Alabama Department of Revenue says property tax is due October 1 and is delinquent after December 31. Its timetable page then lists February for transfer to the probate court, March for the probate court meeting, April for advertising for sale and May for the tax sale.

Some Alabama counties have moved to selling tax liens instead, and the sequence then differs, so read the notice that comes from your own county.

DateAlabama timetable step
October 1Taxes due
January 1Taxes delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to probate court
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

Where do you record a deed or look up records in Birmingham?

Documents go to the Probate Court of Jefferson County, which has a Birmingham division in the courthouse at 716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd. and a Bessemer division at 1801 3rd Avenue North. According to the court's recording FAQ, office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday.

  • Recording staff cannot run a title search or tell you whether liens exist.
  • They cannot prepare or revise a deed. They suggest a lawyer, and name the Birmingham Bar Association as a referral source.
  • Copies made in the Record Room cost $1.00 per page, plats are $15.00 per page, and certification adds $2.00 per document.
  • Recording fees vary, and the office takes cards, cash, cashier's checks, money orders and local personal checks with identification.

Plan a title search before closing on any Birmingham house. A title company or attorney does it, not the recording office, and the results tell you about liens, old mortgages and tax matters before closing day.

How does a cash sale work in Birmingham when tax is owed?

The title company pays the unpaid property tax from your proceeds and records the deed with the probate court. Before you sell, get a payoff figure from the county tax office that issued your bill and give it to the closing agent.

If your house has been through the delinquency calendar, also gather any notices from the probate court or a lien buyer, because those parties may have redemption rights. Our Alabama tax sale page covers redemption windows.

We buy Birmingham houses as they stand. That includes older homes, houses with deferred repairs and houses with tax behind.

More questions about Birmingham, AL Property Tax Guide

What counties is Birmingham in?

Jefferson and Shelby, according to the city's Wikipedia infobox. Birmingham is the county seat of Jefferson County, so most owners deal with Jefferson County offices. Check which county sent your tax bill.

When are property taxes due in Birmingham?

October 1, and they are delinquent after December 31, per the Alabama Department of Revenue.

Where do I record a deed in Birmingham?

At the Probate Court of Jefferson County. The Birmingham division is at 716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd. and the Bessemer division is at 1801 3rd Avenue North.

Can the Jefferson County recording office tell me if I have liens?

No. Its FAQ says employees cannot perform a title search. A title company or attorney can, and the records are open to the public.

What is the biggest employer in the Birmingham area?

UAB, described in the Wikipedia article as the area's largest employer, with about 18,750 workers as of 2011.

What is the elevation of Birmingham?

About 597 feet, per the Wikipedia infobox. The city lies in Jones Valley, with Red Mountain just south of downtown.

Does Birmingham have tornado risk?

Yes. The city lies in Dixie Alley, and the area has seen two F5 tornadoes and an EF4 during the April 2011 outbreak.
